records.recommendation: Leave the owner as it is. The Consumers Energy purchase of this plant did not happen.
records.researcher_notes: CMS Energy and Consumers Energy signed a purchase agreement for Dearborn Industrial Generation in June 2021 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/201533/000110465921084502/tm2120427d1_8k.htm). A press release from the Environmental Law and Policy Center on the 2022 Consumers resource plan settlement (https://elpc.org/news/michigan-energy-regulators-approve-broadly-supported-settlement-on-consumers-energys-long-term-resource-plan/) says the settlement precludes Consumers from buying the plant. In the CMS Energy second quarter 2026 outlook (https://s26.q4cdn.com/888045447/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/CMS-Energy-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-Outlook.pdf), CMS says it keeps Dearborn Industrial Generation inside its NorthStar Clean Energy business. The September 2026 EIA table still lists Dearborn Industrial Gen Inc as the owner. I found no document showing a closed sale to Consumers in 2025, so the brief's premise that U-21090 records that sale was not borne out. I could not read the Michigan Public Service Commission docket directly. The owner company is a CMS NorthStar subsidiary, which a researcher may want to confirm in a CMS annual report.

records.recommendation: Decide whether MISO requests J4159 and J4160 are an expansion at Zeeland or a new plant. If no filing ties them to Zeeland by the next batch, add a new plant in Ottawa County from the queue.

verifications.note: MISO queue data lists J4159 and J4160.

records.researcher_notes: MISO's generator interconnection queue at https://www.misoenergy.org/planning/resource-utilization/GI_Queue/gi-interactive-queue/ lists two gas requests in Ottawa County, both queued on August 13, 2025 and both connecting at the Roosevelt substation on the METC system. J4159 is a 616 MW combined cycle project in the 2026 study cycle with an in-service date of June 30, 2028. Some copies of the queue, such as the Cleanview list at https://cleanview.co/power-projects/planned/natural-gas-power-plants/michigan, give it as 664 MW, likely the winter rating. J4160 is a 55 MW simple cycle gas turbine with an in-service date of May 31, 2026. The rows are copied at https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/miso-j4159 and https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/miso-j4160. Neither request names a developer. The only gas plants GEM has in Ottawa County are Zeeland generating station and Holland energy park. Neither plant's research for this batch found the requests. I could not find which plant the Roosevelt substation serves. A 55 MW turbine with a 2026 date looks like an addition at an existing plant, and the 616 MW request could be a new combined cycle block there. If it is a new site, the 616 MW request meets the add threshold on the queue entry alone.

records.plant_name: University of Michigan central power plant
records.recommendation: No add for now. A reviewer may want to confirm that the campus plant is under the 50 MW threshold.
records.researcher_notes: EIA's monthly generator file for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists EIA plant 50431, University of Michigan, with generators CT6 at 15.5 MW, TG1, TG7 and TG8 at 12.5 MW each, and TG9 and TG10 at 3.5 MW each, all grouped as one combined cycle unit of 60 MW. The state air permit staff report of 2024 at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/-5303010553079006113 describes four gas and oil fired boilers feeding steam turbines, plus combined heat and power gas turbines with heat recovery boilers. Most of the steam turbines run on boiler steam, not turbine exhaust, so they are not part of a combined cycle block. The largest gas turbine with its recovery boiler is well under 50 MW. I treated the plant as below the threshold.
